newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall 4th week in row.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall 4th week in row.

text.p: Average commitment rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages fell a fourth consecutive week in the week ending May 16, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
Thirty-year mortgages fell to an average 7.91 percent in the May 16 week from 7.94 percent the previous week, while 15-year mortgages dipped to 7.44 percent from 7.47 percent.
One-year adjustable rate mortgages fell a fifth consecutive week to 5.78 percent from 5.82 percent last week, Freddie Mac said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.08 percent, the 15-year 7.59 percent and the ARM 5.78 percent.
"Interest rates inched down, though just slightly, this week in part because of speculation about the direction of the economy," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
"When the Federal Reserve meets next week, we may see more definitive movement in the markets, depending on what action the Fed takes," Van Order added.
The Federal Open Market Committee is scheduled to meet on May 20. Many economists are expecting another hike in interest rates next week.

Earlier Thursday the Labor Department said that U.S. April consumer prices rose 0.1 percent, while the Fed reported U.S. industrial production as flat last month and capacity use down to 83.4 percent.
On Wednesday the Labor Department said April producer prices fell 0.6 percent.
Lenders charged an average 1.6 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.4 percent on ARM loans, also unchanged from the previous week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
